newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea Dainong Group ups Midopa stake. [CORRECTED 11:02 GMT 16/3]
newsitem.headline: S.Korea Dainong Group ups Midopa stake. [CORRECTED 11:02 GMT 16/3]

text.p: The Dainong Group's stake in Midopa Department Store Co will rise to 45.5 percent (corrects from 55.17 percent) as it has agreed to buy an additional 12.6 percent (corrects from 22.3 percent) stake in Midopa from other shareholders, statements filed with the Korea Stock Exchange said on Saturday.

Midopa, the nation's major retailer chain, has been the target of a hostile takeover bid by Shindongbang Corp. Market analysts said Dainong's purchase would likely put an end to Shindongbang's takeover effort.

In the statement to the stock exchange, Sungwon Corp (corrects from Sungwon Group) said it had decided to sell its entire 2.97 percent (corrects from 12.63 percent) stake in Midopa to the Dainong Group.
Separately, Daehan Investment Banking Corp also said in a statement it would sell its entire 9.67 percent stake in Midopa to the Dainong Group at 42,000 won per share.
The purchase price is far above Midopa stock's closing price of 23,400 won per share on Saturday.
Shindongbang, along with Dongbang Peregrine Securities and Korea Industrial Co, has accumulated a combined 15.64 percent of Midopa's share capital in the open market.
Meanwhile, Shindongbang said on Saturday in a statement it had considered offering tenders to buy Midopa shares but decided not to do so.
"According to consulations, both parties will maintain a friendly, developmental and cooperative relationship," Shindongbang said in the statement.
A Korea Industrial statement also said it had decided not to offer tenders to buy Midopa and Dainong Co shares, while it has considered doing so.
